title: hello-managed — a multi-tenant gateway daemon (target: managed)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Two tenants, HS256-JWT auth, per-tenant budgets, hash-chained audit logs.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to answer a run.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and the shape — a long-running gateway daemon.”

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: “One agent serves every tenant — and it answers tersely, by instruction.”

beats.label: Declare tenant-a and its budget
beats.cue: “A tenant is an id plus a token budget the gateway enforces on every call.”

beats.label: Declare tenant-b
beats.cue: “Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed — 36 lines, tenants included

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window)

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — one file you own.”

beats.label: Pin the JWT secret
beats.cue: “Set it ahead of time — at least 16 chars — to pin the secret across restarts.”

verify.note: without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it

beats.label: Put tenant storage under live/
beats.cue: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 21 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera.

verify.note: default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it.

verify.note: boots with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-a
beats.cue: The tenant_id claim IS the tenant — HS256 over the secret we just pinned, no key involved.
beats.command: TENANT_A_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-a" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-a
beats.cue: [needs-key] One authenticated call — the client names the session, and runs.create comes back with a runId and the reply.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_A_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"1","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of France?","sessionId":"sess_0123456789abcdef"}}'

verify.note: crewhaus.v1 envelope. Measured with credentials: result.runId=run_…, reply “Paris is the capital of France.”. sessionId is passed explicitly because CLI 0.4.0's managed codegen mints a base36 default id that session-store rejects (expects sess_<16 hex>) — omit it and the gateway answers internal_error. Keyless it answers internal_error too: no Anthropic credentials.

groups.title: One more thing · the invariant target: managed exists to enforce

beats.label: Read tenant-a's audit log
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Hash-chains the audit log so tampering is detectable.” GENESIS → hash → hash → hash.

verify.note: written by the run-create beat. Measured: three records — gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-b
beats.cue: Same secret, same daemon — a different tenant_id, and again no key.
beats.command: TENANT_B_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-b" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless, like run-mint; second tenant declared in the spec's tenants: block

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-b
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same endpoint, second tenant — the daemon rebases its storage on the claim.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_B_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"2","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of Japan?","sessionId":"sess_fedcba9876543210"}}'

verify.note: creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on first authenticated call. Measured: reply “Tokyo is the capital of Japan.”. sessionId explicit for the same 0.4.0 reason as run-create

beats.label: Show the two tenant trees
beats.cue: [needs-key] Two roots. “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.”

verify.note: measured after both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree

beats.label: Stop the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon the run-boot beat backgrounded into this same terminal; skip this and the take leaves a process holding :3000
